job.style: a comparison of two related ideas

passage: Water is a precious resource, yet many people wrongly believe that because Earth is covered in water, we can never run out of usable fresh water. In reality, most of Earth's water is salty, and only a tiny fraction is fresh water available for our needs. Furthermore, rain does not fall equally across our country; some regions receive heavy monsoon showers while others face severe drought. This uneven distribution means that every drop counts, regardless of where we live. Many students think that saving water is only the responsibility of adults or the government, but individual actions make a huge difference. For instance, leaving the tap running while brushing your teeth wastes gallons of water that could have been saved. Similarly, water used for washing vegetables or clothes is not useless; it can be collected and reused for watering plants or cleaning floors. Finally, rainwater harvesting is a vital technique for everyone, not just those in high-rainfall areas. By directing rainwater into underground pits, we can refill our groundwater levels rather than just storing it in surface tanks. Every small effort, from fixing a dripping tap to reusing greywater, helps ensure that we do not exhaust our limited supply of fresh water.

items.evidence: In reality, most of Earth's water is salty, and only a tiny fraction is fresh water available for our needs.
items.q: Earth is covered in water. Why can we still run short of usable water?
options: Very little of it is fresh enough to use
Most of it is frozen in rivers and lakes
Sea water is safe to drink if there is plenty
Rain fills it back up faster than we use it
items.explain: Most of Earth's water is salty, and only a tiny fraction is fresh water we can use.

wrong.why: thinks rivers and lakes hold most of the fresh water
thinks sea water can be used for drinking
thinks rain refills all water so saving is needless

items.evidence: This uneven distribution means that every drop counts, regardless of where we live.
items.q: Town A gets heavy monsoon rain and Town B faces drought. What should people in Town A do?
options: Still save water, since rain is uneven across India
Use water freely, since their town has plenty
Stop saving, since the rain refills everything
Save water only when the monsoon is weak
items.explain: Rain is uneven across the country, so every drop counts everywhere, even where rain is heavy.

wrong.why: thinks all places get the same plentiful rain
thinks rain refills water so saving is needless
thinks saving matters only in dry spells

items.evidence: Similarly, water used for washing vegetables or clothes is not useless; it can be collected and reused for watering plants or cleaning floors.
items.q: Which action shows a good way to reuse water at home?
options: Pouring vegetable-washing water on garden plants
Pouring drinking water on garden plants
Draining washing water straight into the street
Pouring clothes-washing water into the drinking pot
items.explain: Water from washing vegetables or clothes can be collected and reused for watering plants or cleaning floors.

wrong.why: thinks only drinking and bathing water counts as water use
thinks used water drained away is fine as it returns to nature
thinks used water can be used for drinking

items.evidence: By directing rainwater into underground pits, we can refill our groundwater levels rather than just storing it in surface tanks.
items.q: How can rainwater harvesting help the water under the ground?
options: Pits let rain soak down and refill groundwater
Tanks let rain stay stored above the ground
Rain falling on soil turns into drinking water
Groundwater refills by itself as fast as we pump
items.explain: Directing rainwater into underground pits refills groundwater, not just storing it in surface tanks.

wrong.why: thinks harvested rain is only stored in tanks
thinks all rain becomes drinking water
thinks groundwater refills as fast as pumped

items.evidence: Every small effort, from fixing a dripping tap to reusing greywater, helps ensure that we do not exhaust our limited supply of fresh water.
items.q: Why does the passage say fixing a dripping tap is worth doing?
options: Small savings add up to protect limited fresh water
A drip is too small to be worth fixing
Only the government can fix water shortages
Fixed taps make rain fall more evenly
items.explain: Every small effort, even fixing a drip, helps us avoid using up our limited fresh water.

wrong.why: thinks a dripping tap wastes too little to matter
thinks saving water is only the government's job
mixes tap saving up with rainfall spread
